page: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is driven by a quad-core Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, exposing 8 dedicated vCPUs through hyperthreading. The platform features 32 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. A key architectural distinction is its bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing low-latency disk access directly on the physical host. Network baseline throughput is configured at 2 Gbps, and no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data reflects capable middle-tier throughput for multi-core and memory-centric workloads. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 7396.11 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 6989.22. Memory performance is consistent, demonstrating 48.61 GB/sec on large block reads, 36.16 GB/sec on large block writes, and an average PassMark memory score of 2150.77. In simulated server tasks, the machine sustained 6.88 million Redis SET operations per second, 6.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and steady compilation throughput in Clang. Conversely, single-core processing demonstrates lower performance thresholds, with Geekbench single-core scores (1013.0) and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 routines ranking in the bottom quartile. Model inference on medium-sized 7B parameter LLMs also tests poorly due to the lack of dedicated vector or matrix acceleration extensions like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX.

Qualitatively, the m5d.2xlarge provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for production scenarios that demand direct-attached NVMe storage alongside general compute. The tradeoff between moderate single-threaded performance and strong multi-core memory bandwidth makes it practical for multi-threaded enterprise services rather than compute-bound single-thread tasks. The instance is suited for caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis, containerized application hosting, CI/CD build environments, and staging data workloads that benefit from rapid ephemeral storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 32 GB of DDR4 RAM and 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without a discrete GPU and delivers 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate solid mid-tier multi-threaded and memory capabilities, achieving 6.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.93 GB/sec static web serving throughput, alongside average PassMark and Clang compilation metrics. Single-thread processing and AI inference remain modest, with lower-quartile Geekbench single-core and compression marks. The presence of bundled high-speed NVMe storage and a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio positions the m5d.2xlarge effectively for caching tiers, container hosts, CI/CD build environments, and general web workloads needing fast ephemeral storage.
